 Learning about earnings: Can we rely on labour market slack to mitigate the latest supply shock? − speech by Megan Greene
 Learning about earnings: Can we rely on labour market slack to mitigate the latest supply shock? − speech by Megan Greene
 Given at London School of Economics 
 Published on 
 20 October 2026
 The extent to which the latest energy price shock feeds into more persistent inflation through second-round effects remains a key consideration for policymakers. The presence of slack in the labour market could suggest that wage pressures will remain contained, limiting the scope for second-round effects. But is this likely to be the case?
 In this speech, Megan challenges this argument, drawing on a wide range of wage indicators to assess recent developments in pay growth and the likely path ahead for wages and domestically-generated inflation. She then turns to broader measures of labour market slack to examine whether current conditions are likely to restrain second-round effects via the wage-setting channel.
 Speech
 Introduction
 Thank you for inviting me to the LSE to speak. It’s nice to be back here—I often studied in your library when I was an undergraduate in the US working in London for the summer. Come to think of it, I may have snuck in so please don’t alert the authorities. 
 Over the past few months, a lot has happened in the world of geopolitics…and yet very little has fundamentally changed. Passage through the Strait of Hormuz remains beset by attacks and potential new chokepoints in shipping have emerged such as the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Although Middle Eastern oil flows have at times returned to near pre-war levels, expensive and inefficient workarounds have kept energy prices high (Figure 1). Wholesale gas prices are close to triple their level at the start of the year, with oil spot prices just under double their early-January level. footnote [1] And the prices for refined products have remained elevated despite volatile spot prices. Even if the conflict in Iran ends tomorrow, we have already been hit by a protracted energy shock.
 Figure 1: Evolution of energy prices since start of 2026
 Index, 100 = price at 1 Jan 2026
 Footnotes
 Source: ONS, Bloomberg Finance L.P. and Bank calculations.
 (a) Dashed vertical lines denote selected key events. Dates may not be exact due to frequency of data. Latest datapoints are for 19 October 2026.
 I have previously laid out the various avenues via which such a negative supply shock can propagate through the UK economy, highlighting the important role of second-round effects in embedding inflation in the economy. As I set out in my last speech in June, they can take hold through the price- or wage-setting channel, or both. For today’s purposes, I will focus specifically on the wage-setting channel.
 Wages represent a material cost for firms, particularly in the services sector where labour accounts for a large share of total costs. Wages are also a significant determinant of incomes, thus underpinning consumption. As a result, measures of wage growth offer useful insight into domestically-generated inflation. Of course, not all wage growth is inflationary. If wages rise because productivity improves, the implications for inflation may well be limited. But wages can also act as the mechanism through which temporary negative supply shocks become embedded in domestic inflation, particularly when workers seek to protect real incomes and firms then raise prices to protect their margins. 
 The MPC has judged that there is slack in the labour market, as evidenced by the ratio of vacancies to unemployment relative to equilibrium (Figure 2). Some of my colleagues and I have argued that the wage-setting channel poses a smaller risk of generating second-round effects than the price-setting channel. If firms are facing higher costs and have experienced years of margin compression, they are likely to pass on some of their higher costs by raising prices. This is consistent with intelligence that we’re hearing from our Agents. But if there is slack in the labour market, worker power is relatively weak. Even if workers demand higher pay as their costs go up, employers may deny that request given the large pool of talent from which to choose. 
 Figure 2: Vacancy-unemployment (V-U) ratio and V-U equilibrium
 Ratio (a) 
 Footnotes
 Source: Advertising association/ World Advertising Research Centre Expenditure Report, ONS and Bank calculations. Latest data point is for 2026Q2.
 (a) The equilibrium V/U ratio is estimated using an error-correction model over the period 1982–2024. The real cost of vacancy posting and hourly labour productivity are included as long-run determinants for the level of vacancies. The model also includes controls for short-term movements in these variables ( Stelmach, Kensett , & Schnattinger, 2025 )
 Given our monetary policy strategy has relied partly on slack mitigating the impact of second-round effects, it’s worth exploring how much labour market slack there really is. The wider economy has proved surprisingly resilient, implying there is less slack than some labour market indicators suggest. If so, there is a greater risk of second-round effects emerging through the wage-setting channel than we initially thought.
 We may not have a clear steer on whether the shock from the Iran conflict gives rise to material second-round effects through wage- or price-setting until early next year when our Agents’ pay survey is out in February and the brunt of 2027 pay settlements are agreed in January and April. But if we wait for this evidence to lean against second-round effects with a tighter monetary policy stance, we will already be too late given the lags with which monetary policy affects the economy and inflation. 
 As outlined in our Forecast Evaluation Report and the Macro-technical paper alongside it, predicting wage growth has been a challenge for the Bank, particularly since the Global Financial Crisis. As shown in Figure 3, Bank forecasts tended to systematically predict higher wage growth than what we experienced until the Covid period, after which our forecasts systematically underestimated the strength of wage growth. footnote [2] 
 Figure 3: MPR forecasts and outturns of wage growth (a) 
 Annual growth (%) (a) 
 Footnotes
 Source: ONS and Bank calculations.
 (a) The grey lines show forecasts from different vintages. The aqua line shows the outturns k=12 quarters after the first data release.
 Our suite of wage models, like many macro forecasting models, are largely driven by historical relationships. The recent persistent undershooting of wage growth forecasts may suggest something structurally shifted in the labour market during the pandemic. As I argued in my 2024 speech ( Greene, 2024 ), this could reflect reduced matching efficiency, lower search intensity, labour hoarding, persistent recruitment difficulties and weaker participation. It could also reflect stronger real wage resistance following the 2022 energy shock than historical relationships have implied ( Pill, 2025 ). Wage growth has generally decelerated since 2023, suggesting these upward pressures have been unwinding, but they may not have unwound entirely.
 Models inevitably simplify reality, and their performance depends critically on the quality of the signals they are trying to capture. One important development over the past decade has been an expansion in the range of wage indicators we look at, reflecting efforts to measure underlying wage pressures from multiple perspectives.
 But this richer information set has brought its own challenges. At the moment, wage data are like a Rorschach Test; they can be used to confirm anyone’s preconceived view of slack in the labour market because they

植田総裁記者会見(１０月１６日) 
――Ｇ２０終了後の植田総裁、三村財務官 共同記者会見における総裁発言 
２０２６年１０月２０日 
日本銀行 
 
―― 於・バンコク（タイ） 
２０２６年１０月１６日（金） 
午後６時３７分から約２５分間（現地時間） 
 
【冒頭発言】 
会合での議論の内容については財務官の方から様々なご説明があった通りでございます。 私からは
一言だけ、 Ｇ２０では中東情勢あるいはＡＩ関連需要の動向等を受けた経済・物価等への影響あるい
は動きを含め、 世界経済や金融システムなどについて議論が交わされたということをご報告させて頂
きます。 
 
【問】 
植田総裁には、 今回のＧ２０、 ＩＭＦ総会では世界経済のショックに対する頑健性についていろい
ろな声が出た一方で、旺盛なＡＩ需要によるインフレ圧力が話題になったと思います。今回の会合で
の議論は 10 月の展望レポートでの議論や今後の利上げパスについての議論にどう影響するのでしょ
うか。 日銀は物価の上振れリスクの高まりを重視して9 月に利上げしましたが、 こうやって世界的に
高まるインフレ圧力を考えると、また近いうちに更なる追加利上げが必要な環境というふうにお考え
でしょうか。 
 
【答】 
世界経済のインフレ圧力のようなものについて何か示唆があったかどうか、 それが私どもの今後の
政策にインプリケーションがあるかどうかというご質問だったと思いますけれども、 まずインフレ圧
力そのものについては、私ども暫く前から、円安に加えて中東情勢とＡＩ関連の動向というものを注
視するということを申し上げてきた通りです。特に中東とＡＩは世界全体に影響する話で、従って、
詳しく私どもも分析してきましたし、今回の様々な会合で世界の政策担当者と議論したわけですが、
われわれとその他の政策担当者の間で大きな食い違いはないという印象を持ったところです。 あえて
申し上げれば、ＡＩ関連の需要動向について、私どもがみていたよりも、やや心持ちしっかりしてい
る、需要そのものですね、というふうにみてらっしゃる方が少し多いかなというふうに思ったところ
です。 こうしたことの私どもの政策への含意ですけれども、 基本姿勢を申し上げることにとどまりま
2 
 
すけれども、基調的な物価上昇率が2％に近づいている中で、一方で金融環境がいつも申し上げてい
る通り緩和的な状態が続いているということですので、 基本的には引き続き政策金利を、経済 ・ 物価 ・
金融情勢に応じてですけれども、引き上げて、緩和度合いを調整していくというふうになると考えて
います。そのうえで、タイミングやペースについては、今申し上げたような中東、ＡＩ関連の需要の
動向、 あるいは為替相場の動き、これをみながら私どもの見通しの確度やその周りのリスクを点検し
ながら検討していくということです。9 月の決定会合後の会見で申し上げたことと重なりますけれど
も、その際に、基調物価が 2％にかなり接近しているという中では、基調物価の上昇率を 2％程度で
安定させていくという観点がこれまでよりも重要になってくるというふうに考えております。 そうい
うことを考えつつ、適切に政策を判断してまいりたいと思っております。 
 
【問】 
植田総裁に伺います。若干、今の質問と関連するんですけれども、一連の会議やバイ会談で様々な
政策当局者の方と意見交換されたと思うんですけれども、 私も10 月30 日に新しい展望レポートが出
るっていうことを念頭に伺いたいんですけれども、先ほど、ＡＩ需要のところがもともとみているよ
りは心持ちしっかりしてるっていうような所感をおっしゃってらっしゃいましたけれども、 中心的見
通しやリスク要因の記述を考えるときに、これまでのシナリオを変更するような必要性というか、 新
しい発見みたいなところっていうのはあったのでしょうか。 
あと、 基調物価上昇率に関してなんですけれども、 こちらも今まで展望レポートで、2026 年度後半
から 27 年度にかけて 2％目標と整合的な水準になるっていうふうに見通しを示してこられましたけ
れども、10 月会合で 26 年度後半というところに入ってきます。ここの記載ぶりというのはその見通
し期間に入ってきたところで変える可能性はあるとお考えでしょうか。 
 
【答】 
私どもの中心的な見通しを変えるようなニュースがあったかどうかという点ですけれども、まず9
月の決定会合後の日本経済周りのデータをみる限りは、概ね私どもの見通し通りに動いているという
ふうに考えています。今回の会合で様々な意見交換をしましたけれども、 そういうことと矛盾するよ
うな重要な情報がもたらされたというふうには考えておりません。 
それから基調物価の判断について、10 月の決定会合でどういうふうに記述するかということです
けれども、今のところ 2％にかなり近づいているっていう表現ぶりでありますけれども、これをどう
いうふうにするかということについては、 これは申し訳ありませんが、10 月の会合でそこまでに得ら
れた情報をもとに、政策委員の間でしっかり議論して結論を出したいと思っております。 
 
【問】 
植田総裁に私も二問ほど質問させてください。まず一問目なんですが、今回の一連の会合ではベッ
セント米財務長官が欠席されましたので、対面でお話しする機会はなかったと思うんですけれども、
アシュビルのＧ２０以降の機会で何かコミュニケーションをとられるような場面はあったのかとい
うのを伺いたいのが一点です。 
3 
 
もう一つは先ほどの質問にも関連するところなんですが、 基調的な物価上昇率が2％に達している、
こういった判断を次回、 今月の会合でも一部同じ政策委員の方とお話しされるかなと思うんですけれ
ども、もし物価上昇率が 2％に達していると判断された場合、それは金融政策を判断するうえでどの
ようなインプリケーションがありますでしょうか。例えば、比較的速いペースで利上げを進める必要
があるですとか、そういった意味を持つことなんでしょうか。 
 
【答】 
ベッセント長官とはアシュビル以降、コミュニケーションは特にとっておりません。 
それから二番目は、基調物価に関する表現ぶりをどうするかということは先ほどのご質問もあった
ところですけれども、それは 10 月の決定会合の議論を待たないと、何とも私から今の時点では申し
上げられません。ただし、既にかなり基調物価は 2％に近づいているということは私も含めて申し上
げてきた通りで、それは前回の会合で、ある種、政策の局面が変化したということであるというふう
に申し上げてきています。その意味は先ほどもちらっと申し上げましたけれども、これまでは基調物
価を少しずつ 2％に近づけていくという意味で上がる、下から来ていますので、という方向の動きを
容認してきたわけですけれども、今後は2％に概ね近いということで、これ以上上がるということは
容認できない、2％近辺で定着していくということを政策の大きな目標にするという姿勢に、最近局
面が変化したということでございます。 
 
【問】 
植田総裁にお伺いさせてください。 先ほどもこれまでのＧ２０、Ｇ７とかの会合を踏まえてお話も
ありましたけども、 植田総裁として一連の日程を振り返って、今回の成果として挙げられる部分とい
うのはどういったところになるのか、 例えばどういった意見交換をしたっていうところが大きな示唆
を得たとか、その辺り、成果としてとらえてらっしゃる部分があればお願いします。 
 
【答】 
具体的なことはなかなか申し上げられないので、抽象的な一般論になってしまいますけれども、 先
ほど来申し上げてますような中東情勢あるいはＡＩ周りの動き、 こういうことが世界経済、 日本経済、
あるいはそれぞれのインフレ動向にどういうルートを通じてどういうふうに影響するのかというこ
とについて、私どもも海外の政策担当者も様々な意見、情報を持ってるわけですが、それをお互いに
議論して情報を交換し合う、それによってわれわれの判断をよりしっかりしたものにする、そして次
の政策に役立てていく、 こういう場として私どもは活用させて頂いてますし、それは海外の政策担当
者も同じであるというふうに思っています。 
 
【問】 
植田総裁に二問質問させてください。今回ベッセント氏は欠席されましたが、ＦＲＢのウォーシュ
議長は出席しましたが、何かコミュニケーションなどはあったんでしょうかというのが一点。 
もう一点が中立金利についてですけれど、 政策金利1.25％到達してますが、 中立金利にはまだ相応
4 
 
の距離があると考えていらっしゃいますか。その辺りの少し考えをお伺いしたいです。 
 
【答】 
ウォーシュ議長とはもちろん立ち話や会合の中の意見交換を含めて、様々な意見交換を致しました。
具体的な内容については差し控えさせて頂きます。 
それから中立金利に関してですけれども、これはこれまでも申し上げています通り、 はっきりとこ
の辺にある、ここにあるっていうことを申し上げられるような材料があるわけではない一方で、これ
までの利上げの累積的な効果、 金融環境および経済・物価へどういう影響が累積的な効果として出て
きているかということをみながら、一歩一歩判断していきたいというふうに考えています。 
以 上

 Governor's Special Address at the 21st Kuala Lumpur Islamic Finance Forum (KLIFF 2026)
 Special Address by Governor Dato’ Sri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour
at the 21st Kuala Lumpur Islamic Finance Forum (KLIFF) 2026
Kuala Lumpur | 20 October 2026 
 'Islamic Finance for Impact – The Next Measure of Success' 
 It is a pleasure to be here at the 21st Kuala Lumpur Islamic Finance Forum.
 From scale to impact 
 Over the last five decades, Islamic finance has demonstrated its capacity to grow. Our first steps were to build credibility, strong foundations, and scale. At the midpoint, the focus shifted towards strengthening competitiveness, innovation, and capabilities.
 Today, the context is markedly different. Economies are confronting climate risks, demographic change, wider developmental needs and geopolitical fragmentation. These forces are reshaping our economies and financing needs.
 This year’s theme for KLIFF speaks directly to this task. It invites us to look beyond scale and consider outcomes. It raises the standard by which Islamic finance should now be measured. The challenge is to demonstrate not only continued strength, but greater relevance to the economies and societies it serves.
 The question before us today can no longer simply be: “Can Islamic finance compete and grow?”. Rather, we must ask a more consequential question:
 'What does that growth now enable?'
'What opportunities can it create?'
'What outcomes can it deliver?'
 At the recent Financial Institutions Directors' Education (FIDE) programme, I asked whether we are still financing yesterday's economy or positioning ourselves for Malaysia’s next phase of growth. Today, I want to take that conversation one step further. Not just what Islamic finance should finance. But what that should achieve and how do we measure our success.
 Redefining the measure of success 
 This focus on outcomes is not new. It is rooted in the foundations of Islamic finance. History reminds us that finance was not understood as an end in itself, but as a means of supporting broader economic and societal objectives. The legitimacy of financial activity was closely connected to the value it created beyond individual transactions.
 Consider the great külliye complexes of the Ottoman Empire [1] – including the remarkable Süleymaniye Complex. Sustained through waqf , they brought together schools, hospitals, libraries, welfare services, and commerce.
 They were not just a collection of buildings. They were a complete ecosystem built around a mosque, designed to create lasting societal outcomes. Success was measured by the greater purpose it sought:
 to improve education;
 to enhance health services;
 to enable more upward social mobility; and
 to strengthen community wellbeing across generations.
 There is an important lesson here: The resources mattered, but the outcomes mattered more.
 This calls for us to widen our measure of success:
 From assets to outcomes;
 From transactions to transformation;
 From financial inclusion to meaningful economic participation;
 From Shariah compliance to the fulfilment of Shariah purpose; and
 From growth of finance to growth enabled by finance.
 These measures represent an evolution in how we understand role of finance and its contributions to society and economy.
 Finance that empowers 
 This perspective is especially relevant in the context of financial inclusion and economic participation, where financial access itself should not be viewed as the final and desired outcome. This matters in Malaysia, where Micro, Small and Medium enterprises (MSMEs) contributed almost 40% of GDP [2] and accounted for almost 50% of total employment in 2025 – with more than three-quarters of them are microenterprises. Yet, many of these businesses continue to face challenges beyond access to finance.
 Today, Malaysia’s social finance initiative, iTEKAD [3] offers a practical illustration. At first glance, it is a social finance programme. But financing alone does not create empowerment. Sustainable, lasting empowerment requires:
 financing and protection,
 financing and capability,
 financing and access to markets.
 Put together, these elements help microentrepreneurs build stronger and more sustainable livelihoods. It addresses the interconnected constraints that can prevent low-income entrepreneurs from sustaining and expanding their businesses.
 iTEKAD has supported nearly sixteen thousand participants through its entrepreneurship, employment, and protection programmes. But its impact is best understood through the lives it transformed. Let me share the story of Puan Fauziah, a microentrepreneur from Klang.
 Puan Fauziah began with a home-based business selling traditional ginger floss for postpartum mothers. Like many, she had determination. What she lacked were the resources to grow. Through iTEKAD’s grant financing and entrepreneurship training, her business expanded. Today, she reaches customers through digital platforms and has even exported to the United Kingdom through a halal marketplace.
 That is the outcome that matters. A stronger livelihood, greater resilience and upward economic mobility.
 This also brings us to an equally important consideration on capital allocation. Capital is never passive. Every financing decision shapes the economy. It influences which sectors expand, which businesses grow and which innovations receive support. Capital allocation is therefore an act of stewardship of the nation’s economy.
 Strengthening Malaysia’s productive capacity requires capital to flow to the right places. Traditional approaches may no longer be sufficient. Islamic finance can provide innovative risk-sharing solutions, especially where broader capital sources, structures and different risk profiles are needed. Through i-CITA, launched in 2025, Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) is facilitating industry learning in offering risk-sharing solutions for key areas such as food security and climate resilience.
 Collective stewardship, greater impact 
 These challenges cannot be addressed through isolated efforts. Impact must be a shared endeavour. Regulators, financial institutions, Shariah scholars, and the wider industry must work together to build the ecosystem that impactful innovation requires.
 At BNM, our role is to enable innovation, support responsible risk-taking and create a conducive environment for impactful solutions. The Digital Asset Innovation Hub launched in June 2025 provides one platform for the industry to explore emerging technologies and use cases with real economic value.
 We are also reviewing the Shariah Contract Framework to promote broader and more effective application of Shariah contracts. We will be issuing a Strategy Paper and Exposure Draft this year.
 The next Financial Sector Blueprint will also carry this broader shift. We want to align the financial sector more closely with Malaysia's future socioeconomic priorities. Our measure of success must also evolve in tandem.
 As we look ahead, three priorities warrant our focus:
 First, align strategies and capital with purpose. This means directing resources towards higher-value sectors and renewable energy and strengthening resilience against climate and economic shocks.
 Second, innovate around real needs. We want to build on existing efforts to design solutions around the realities faced by households, and businesses, particularly where needs remain underserved or unmet. This includes financial and technical support for the expansion of halal MSMEs.
 Third, keep values at the centre. Fairness, integrity, empathy. These values must remain central to business decisions and market conduct. Maqasid Shariah is our compass. We want to get to impactful value-based outcomes.
 Islamic finance has travelled far. 
 It has built scale.
It has built sophistication. 
It has built credibility.
 Now, the next measure of success is where we go from here. 
 A more productive economy.
More resilient communities. 
More widely shared opportunities. 
 Scale tells us how far we have travelled. Purpose must remain as our true north to a better future.
 That, in my view, is the next measure of success for Islamic finance.
 Bank Negara Malaysia
20 October 2026 
 [1] Avcıoğlu, N. (2024). The Külliye as hypotext: A new reading of Ottoman imperial mosques and tombs. Journal of Material Cultures in the Muslim World, 4(2), 230–251
 [2] Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM), Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) Performance 2025.
 [3] iTEKAD Entrepreneurship was launched in 2020, iTEKAD Protection in 2025, while iTEKAD Employment was launched in July 2026.

 中央銀行新聞稿 115年10月22日發布
 （115）新聞發布第170號
 115年9月五大銀行新承做放款平均利率 
 本(115)年9月本國五大銀行(台銀、合庫銀、一銀、華銀及土銀)新承做放款加權平均利率為2.193％，較8月的2.187％上升0.006個百分點，係因除購屋貸款利率下降外，其餘各類貸款利率均上升。若不含國庫借款，9月五大銀行新承做放款加權平均利率為2.214％，亦較8月的2.187％上升0.027個百分點。

 業務聯繫單位：經濟研究處金融統計科 電話：(02)2357-1741

 本新聞稿下一次發布時間為115年11月20日下午4時20分
